definition.name: The Reluctant One — becoming who you are by refusing the name until you can own it
definition.theme_or_dilemma: Identity — Who am I, really? The story strips one name off a man ('Anderson') and presses another ('the One') onto him, but suspends the label between destiny and self-creation so that Neo must choose the identity rather than merely receive it.
definition.summary: A man haunted by a nameless dread is told by a disembodied voice that he is 'the One' and asked for a single 'Yes' before he has any grounds to believe it (ev-008), then spends the story actively rejecting that title — denying he is the One even as he commits to a rescue with no prophetic guarantee (ev-032). He is trained, tested, and broken (ev-015, ev-016), and only after dying and being revived does he seize the identity for himself, halting bullets and reading the room as code (ev-045). The causal chain runs from imposed label to refused label to earned identity: he becomes the One precisely by refusing to accept it on anyone else's authority, and finally claiming it on his own terms (ev-047). The plot resolves the dilemma by arguing that identity is not a prophecy fulfilled but a self-chosen act — 'the One' is something he does, not something he is told he is.

chain.why_in_plot: This is the plot's ignition: a disembodied voice names Neo 'the One' and demands a single 'Yes' before he has any grounds to believe it (ev-008) — the imposed label the whole throughline reacts against.
chain.caused_by_previous: First link in the chain; sets it in motion. The name is pressed onto him here, creating the identity he will spend the story refusing.

chain.why_in_plot: Morpheus reframes Neo's 'lifelong, nameless dread' as real and offers the choice to know — the moment the label-bearer commits to guiding him toward the identity Neo still hasn't accepted.
chain.caused_by_previous: The reclaiming and naming in ev-008 delivers Neo to Morpheus's crew, enabling Morpheus to reframe the dread and offer the red pill that begins converting an imposed name into a destiny.

chain.why_in_plot: Morpheus explicitly 'reframes the rescue as destiny by recounting the myth of the One and the Oracle's prophecy' and declares 'the search is over' — the full weight of the 'the One' label being pressed onto Neo.
chain.caused_by_previous: Having survived the shock of the real world (ev-011–013), Neo is now recoverable and present, which enables Morpheus to install the prophetic identity before training begins.

chain.why_in_plot: The 'trained, tested, and broken' phase: Neo downloads skills and is 'beaten to the floor' by Morpheus — the testing that the plot says precedes his earning of the identity.
chain.caused_by_previous: Morpheus's commitment to guide him into training in ev-014 directly enables the combat program and physical dismantling of Neo's self-image here.

chain.why_in_plot: Continuation of being 'broken': Neo runs and 'falls badly short' of the jump, the yielding ground catching him — the failure that keeps him from accepting the One identity on anyone's authority but his own.
chain.caused_by_previous: The sparring defeat in ev-015 establishes the pattern of testing; Morpheus now moves to a rooftop jump to prove the mind governs the Construct, extending the same breaking process.

chain.why_in_plot: Cypher 'recasts Morpheus's prophecy as a body count' and Neo 'retreats... shaken rather than converted' — direct pressure on whether Neo will believe the imposed identity, which he still refuses.
chain.caused_by_previous: The prophecy-installation (ev-014) and failed tests (ev-015–016) make Neo vulnerable to doubt, enabling Cypher to weaponize the 'five before you died' history against Morpheus's faith.

chain.why_in_plot: On the way to the Oracle, Neo 'presses Morpheus over the five failed candidates' and Morpheus confesses he 'misunderstood the Oracle' — the prophecy/identity framework being scrutinized before Neo rejects it on his own terms.
chain.caused_by_previous: Cypher's doubt-seeding (ev-020) primes Neo to interrogate the prophecy rather than receive it, driving the confrontation about the failed candidates here.

chain.why_in_plot: The plot's pivot: Neo 'denies being the One,' so his rescue of Morpheus 'becomes a wager on a man rather than a prophecy' — the active rejection of the label even while committing to a heroic act.
chain.caused_by_previous: The Oracle's private verdict and death-prophecy (ev-023) plus Morpheus's capture force Neo to act; he chooses to rescue Morpheus while explicitly refusing the identity, converting destiny into a self-chosen gamble.

chain.why_in_plot: After the rescue, Morpheus 'reinterprets both the prophecy and Trinity's silence as confirmation' — the external world insisting on the label Neo still denies, keeping the identity suspended between destiny and self-creation.
chain.caused_by_previous: Neo's successful rescue despite his self-denial (ev-032) gives Morpheus the evidence he seizes to reaffirm the prophecy, deepening the tension between imposed and chosen identity.

chain.why_in_plot: Neo 'does not run' but 'hardens into a fixed, gunfighter's calm,' and Morpheus 'reads that stillness as the beginning of belief' — Neo acting as the One without yet claiming the name, the earned-identity trajectory advancing.
chain.caused_by_previous: Trapped alone with Smith after the others escape (ev-037), Neo has no prophecy to lean on; his refusal to flee is the self-chosen stance that Morpheus reads as nascent belief.

chain.why_in_plot: At the edge of death Neo 'refuses the name and fate Smith pronounces' and 'summons an impossible surge' — the plot's core argument that he becomes the One by refusing it on another's authority.
chain.caused_by_previous: His decision to stand and fight (ev-038) leads directly into the battle where Smith tries to fix his death as 'settled inevitability,' provoking Neo's self-authored surge.

chain.why_in_plot: Neo is shot and killed, then revived by Trinity's refusal to accept the ending — the death-and-revival the plot names as the precondition for him finally seizing the identity.
chain.caused_by_previous: His flight to the phone (ev-043) ends with Smith's point-blank shot; the killing is the breaking-point that must precede the awakening.

chain.why_in_plot: The earned identity arrives: revived, Neo 'halts the Agents' volley,' reads 'the room as flowing code,' and destroys Smith from within — 'the One' as something he now does, not something he was told he is.
chain.caused_by_previous: Death and revival (ev-044) enable the awakening; the miracle is what lets him seize the power and, with it, the identity on his own terms.

chain.why_in_plot: Resolution of the dilemma: transformed and 'no longer running,' Neo rises 'into open flight above the skyscrapers' — identity fully self-chosen and owned, closing the arc from imposed label to refused label to earned identity.
chain.caused_by_previous: Having awakened as the One and destroyed Smith (ev-045) and escaped (ev-046), Neo now acts from the identity rather than toward it, completing the self-creation the plot argues for.

definition.name: The Rescue — risking a life you cannot justify to save a man you cannot save by logic
definition.theme_or_dilemma: Self-preservation vs. self-sacrifice — flee to save your own life, or risk it to save another's. Both horns are priced: choosing self costs Morpheus his life and Neo his emerging self-respect; choosing sacrifice costs Neo any claim to safety on a bet
definition.summary: Morpheus first models the sacrifice horn by pinning an Agent and ordering Trinity to get Neo out, giving his own life so the others escape (ev-025), and is then captured and tortured to the brink of breaking (ev-031). Faced with the crew's decision to pull Morpheus's plug, Neo stops it and commits to going back into a world that will kill him to pull out a man he cannot save by any logic, explicitly denying he is the One so the mission is a wager on a man rather than a prophecy (ev-032). This choice conditions everything that follows — the helicopter assault, the mid-dive catch of Morpheus's handcuffed wrist (ev-034), and ultimately Neo's own death and revival, which are the price of having chosen to re-enter (ev-044, ev-045). The plot resolves the dilemma by having Neo pay the full cost of the sacrifice horn and survive it, converting faith into fact.

chain.why_in_plot: This is the plot's founding act of the sacrifice horn: Morpheus pins an Agent and orders Trinity to get Neo out, giving his own life so the others escape — exactly the self-sacrifice the summary names as the model for what follows.
chain.caused_by_previous: As the first link, it is set in motion by the trap closing on the crew (the firefight in the wall), which forces Morpheus to choose to hold the line so Neo can live.

chain.why_in_plot: It delivers the second horn the plot is built on — Morpheus captured and tortured to the brink of breaking — creating the 'man who cannot be saved by logic' that the dilemma requires.
chain.caused_by_previous: It is the direct consequence of ev-025's sacrifice succeeding in intent but failing in outcome: Morpheus gives himself so Neo escapes, and that captured-and-interrogated body is what the Agents now drive toward breaking.

chain.why_in_plot: This is the plot's decisive turn: Neo stops Morpheus's plug from being pulled and commits to re-entering a world that will kill him, explicitly denying he is the One so the rescue is a wager on a man rather than a prophecy — the dilemma's sacrifice horn chosen and priced.
chain.caused_by_previous: It is caused by ev-031's brink-of-breaking torture: seeing Morpheus about to crack is what reverses the wake and forces Neo's impossible, illogical commitment.

chain.why_in_plot: It is the sacrifice horn paid in action — the helicopter assault and the mid-dive catch of Morpheus's handcuffed wrist — the mission Neo committed to in ev-032, risking his life to pull out a man logic says is lost.
chain.caused_by_previous: It is enabled by ev-032's commitment: having chosen to go back, Neo and the crew load the assault and execute the rescue that choice demanded.

chain.why_in_plot: It is the price of having chosen to re-enter — Neo shot and killed, the cost the summary says the sacrifice horn exacts — and the beginning of its conversion of faith into fact.
chain.caused_by_previous: It follows from ev-034's rescue: having gone back in to save Morpheus, Neo is now cornered and gunned down, the direct cost of the re-entry he willed.

chain.why_in_plot: It completes the plot's resolution — Neo's revival, the survival of the sacrifice that the summary says 'converts faith into fact' — confirming the wager on the man rather than the prophecy.
chain.caused_by_previous: It is caused by ev-044's death-and-kiss: Trinity's refusal to accept the ending and the monitors jumping back to life are what let Neo return as the One, closing the dilemma by paying the full cost and surviving it.

definition.name: The Descent into the Real — swallowing the truth and refusing to go back to the lie
definition.theme_or_dilemma: Truth vs. a comfortable lie — is it better to know an unbearable reality or to live a pleasant illusion? The honest answer costs Neo his old world and nearly his sanity, while the counter-argument (Cypher) chooses to be re-plugged into the lie.
definition.summary: Neo's lifelong dread is reframed as an enslaving system and he is offered two exits — forget or know — and he swallows the red pill (ev-010), then recoils as the world is revealed to be a simulation and humans farmed for power, an unbearable violation (ev-013). Morpheus then reframes even this horror as destiny through the myth of the One (ev-014), giving the truth a purpose that makes it endurable. The trap that springs from a rewritten Matrix (ev-023) and Cypher's betrayal — savoring an impossible steak and bargaining to be returned to ignorant comfort (ev-020) — dramatize the counter-argument made flesh. The plot resolves by having Neo hold the unbearable truth without retreating, so that knowing reality becomes the ground on which he later reads the Matrix as code and masters it (ev-045).

chain.why_in_plot: This is the plot's inciting choice: Morpheus reframes Neo's lifelong dread as an enslaving system and offers the two exits (forget/know), and Neo swallows the red pill — exactly the 'swallow the truth' motion the plot names. The summary pins this as ev-010.
chain.caused_by_previous: This is the first link. It is set moving by the accumulated pressure of ev-004–ev-009 (the summons toward truth, the failed ordinary-life reassertion of ev-005, the office seizure, the interrogation, and the bug-implant of ev-007), which funnel Neo to the point where the only way out is to choose to

chain.why_in_plot: The physical consequence of the pill: Neo is expelled from the pod into the real world — the 'world is revealed' motion beginning. It is the direct bodily result of ev-010's choice.
chain.caused_by_previous: The red pill of ev-010 liquefies the mirror and traces Neo's location, forcing the crew to unplug him; ev-011 is that unplugging — ruptured amnion, severed cables, flushed into the sewer — the truth made physically real.

chain.why_in_plot: The plot's central unbearable violation: Morpheus walks Neo through the truth that the world is a simulation and humans are farmed for power, and Neo recoils — explicitly named as ev-013 in the summary.
chain.caused_by_previous: Having been born into the real world (ev-011) and rebuilt (ev-012), Neo is now jacked into the Construct where Morpheus can show him what that world actually is; ev-013 is the delivered payoff of the knowing he chose in ev-010.

chain.why_in_plot: The plot's counter-motion: Morpheus reframes the horror as destiny through the myth of the One, giving the truth a purpose that makes it endurable — explicitly named as ev-014 in the summary.
chain.caused_by_previous: Neo has just recoiled from the unbearable truth in ev-013 (his mind cannot hold it); ev-014 answers that near-break by supplying meaning — the prophecy — so the truth becomes survivable rather than merely shocking.

chain.why_in_plot: The counter-argument made flesh: Cypher savors an impossible steak and bargains to be re-plugged into ignorant comfort — explicitly named as ev-020 in the summary as the 'refuse to know / go back to the lie' position.
chain.caused_by_previous: The plot needs the truth to be shown as genuinely unbearable before the retreat is credible; ev-013 (unbearable violation) plus ev-014 (faith-based reframing) set up Cypher's rejection — he refuses Morpheus's myth and chooses the lie, dramatizing the alternative Neo must not take.

chain.why_in_plot: The trap that springs from a rewritten Matrix — explicitly named as ev-023 in the summary. The rewriting exposes the simulation's falseness, testing whether the crew (and Neo) can hold the truth under assault.
chain.caused_by_previous: Cypher's deal in ev-020 (dropping the traceable phone, bargaining with Smith) is what enables the Matrix to be rewritten around the crew and the trap to close; the betrayal is the mechanism that turns the revealed truth into a lethal ambush.

chain.why_in_plot: The plot's resolution: Neo holds the unbearable truth without retreating, so that knowing reality becomes the ground on which he reads the Matrix as code and masters it — explicitly named as ev-045 in the summary.
chain.caused_by_previous: After the trap (ev-023), the betrayal (ev-029), the death-and-revival sequence (ev-044), Neo has fully absorbed reality without fleeing into the lie; ev-045 is the payoff — he halts the volley and reads the room as flowing code, the mastery that only 'swallowing the truth' makes possible.

definition.name: The Fall of the Disbeliever — measuring a cause only in deaths and trading it for comfort
definition.theme_or_dilemma: Meaning vs. pleasure — a life of purposeful struggle or empty satisfaction? Cypher recasts Morpheus's prophecy as 'a body count' and trades a hard, meaningful freedom for a soft, meaningless comfort, serving as the story's counter-argument to Neo's
definition.summary: Cypher pours out his resentment, recasts the prophecy as a body count (ev-020), and covertly drops a phone in an alley to signal the Agents (ev-021), setting in motion the trap that kills Mouse and captures Morpheus (ev-023, ev-026). His bargain for re-insertion into the Matrix conditions the betrayal aboard the ship — shooting Tank, murdering Apoc and Switch, and delivering Morpheus to the Agents (ev-029) — which in turn forces the crew's wake to be interrupted and reversed into Neo's rescue mission (ev-032). The causal chain is one of escalating treachery that nearly destroys the crew from within. The plot resolves when Tank, left for dead, returns and strikes Cypher down (ev-029), so the counter-argument is answered not by debate but by the death of the man who chose pleasure over purpose.

chain.why_in_plot: Cypher explicitly recasts Morpheus's prophecy as 'a body count' and strikes a private bargain with Agent Smith over an impossible steak — the plot's counter-argument (purposeful struggle vs. soft comfort) is stated and the treachery is set in motion.
chain.caused_by_previous: This is the chain's first link: it opens the betrayal rather than following from an earlier event in this plot.

chain.why_in_plot: Cypher covertly connects a phone and drops it in a garbage can in the alley — the physical act of signaling the Agents that turns his private deal into an operational trap.
chain.caused_by_previous: Enabled by the bargain struck in ev-020: having agreed to trade the crew, he now plants the beacon that will spring the trap.

chain.why_in_plot: The planted signal closes as a trap: Mouse is cornered and killed and Morpheus is forced to seize a traceable phone — the first deaths of the 'body count' Cypher predicted, directly serving his betrayal.
chain.caused_by_previous: Caused by the dropped phone in ev-021: the beacon lets the Agents rewrite the Matrix around the crew and seal them in.

chain.why_in_plot: Cypher surfaces among the fleeing crew, and Morpheus is captured — completing the trap's intended outcome (delivering Morpheus) and advancing Cypher's side of the bargain.
chain.caused_by_previous: Flows from the sealed building and Morpheus's sacrificial rearguard in ev-023/ev-025: the trap forces the crew into the walls and basement where Cypher rejoins them and Morpheus is taken.

chain.why_in_plot: Cypher reaches the exit first and awakens aboard the ship, drawing a concealed rifle — positioning himself to convert the field betrayal into murder aboard the Nebuchadnezzar.
chain.caused_by_previous: Enabled by Morpheus's capture in ev-026 and the crew's flight to the TV-repair-shop exit: Cypher gets ahead of the survivors to prepare the ship-side of the treachery.

chain.why_in_plot: Cypher's treachery peaks into open murder — shooting Tank, killing Apoc and Switch, delivering Morpheus to the Agents, and threatening Neo — the full 'escalating treachery' that nearly destroys the crew from within.
chain.caused_by_previous: Caused by Cypher awakening armed aboard the ship in ev-028: with the survivors jacking back in one by one, he executes the shipboard massacre his earlier deal required.

chain.why_in_plot: The betrayal's fallout interrupts the crew's wake and reverses it into Neo's rescue mission — the plot's stated consequence, where Cypher's actions force the story's response.
chain.caused_by_previous: Follows from the massacre in ev-029: with Morpheus handed to the Agents and the crew decimated, the wake is broken and Neo commits to bringing Morpheus back.

definition.name: The Hunter and the Chosen — a program enforcing inevitability against a man who keeps choosing
definition.theme_or_dilemma: Freedom vs. determinism (fate) — do we choose, or is the path already written? Smith pronounces Neo's death as settled inevitability, and the prophecy of the One sets a pre-scripted world, yet the characters keep acting against the script.
definition.summary: Smith lays out Neo's two lives and offers to erase the 'Anderson' record in exchange for Morpheus, treating Neo as a solvable equation (ev-007), then pursues him as the one variable that will not resolve. At the point of death in the subway, Smith frames Neo's end as settled inevitability and pronounces his name and fate, but Neo refuses the name, summons an impossible surge, and breaks free — the story's loudest claim that choice overrides destiny (ev-039). Smith's fixation then detaches him from his unit (ev-036, ev-042) and drives the final confrontation that ends with Neo entering Smith and bursting out of him, destroying the first Agent ever (ev-045). The plot resolves the dilemma by having the man who was supposed to be pre-scripted overwrite the program that tried to define him.

chain.why_in_plot: This is the plot's seed: Smith lays out Neo's two lives and treats him as a solvable equation (the 'Anderson' record), offering to erase it, then enforces the script by sealing Neo's mouth — the program defining the man. The summary names this as the opening move ('ev-007').
chain.caused_by_previous: First link in the chain; it sets the hunter-vs-chosen conflict in motion by having Smith pronounce Neo a definable, erasable record.

chain.why_in_plot: The story's loudest claim that choice overrides destiny: at the point of death Smith frames Neo's end as settled inevitability and pronounces his name/fate, but Neo refuses the name, summons an impossible surge, and breaks free. Directly cited in the summary ('ev-039').
chain.caused_by_previous: Smith's fixation detaches him from his unit (he withdraws alone into the subway, ev-036), leaving Neo trapped one-on-one with the hunter (ev-037), which produces the death-framing duel where Neo first refuses the script.

chain.why_in_plot: Smith's fixation visibly detaches him from his unit: while the others pursue the trace, Smith's focus locks onto the 'Heart O' The City Hotel' sign, fixing him at a private point of identification. Cited in the summary as the detachment beat ('ev-036, ev-042').
chain.caused_by_previous: Having broken free in the subway (ev-039) and fled (ev-041), Neo is driven back toward the hotel, and Smith's obsession — not his unit's orders — pulls him to that same place, narrowing the world to hunter vs. chosen.

chain.why_in_plot: The chase compresses to its final one-on-one: Neo races to door 303 (echoing the 'Anderson' identity Smith tried to erase) and is stopped cold by Smith's point-blank shot — the variable that won't resolve cornered by the program.
chain.caused_by_previous: Smith's fixation locking onto the hotel (ev-042) puts him exactly where Neo's flight ends, so the hunter is waiting at the finish of the chase.

chain.why_in_plot: Smith pronounces the ending — three shots, death confirmed by Brown — enacting inevitability; but Neo refuses it as Trinity's kiss returns him, the man overriding the sentence written for him.
chain.caused_by_previous: Smith's point-blank shot that stops Neo at door 303 (ev-043) is the 'settled' killing that the miracle then reverses.

chain.why_in_plot: The dilemma resolved: the man who was pre-scripted overwrites the program that tried to define him — Neo enters Smith and bursts out, destroying the first Agent ever. Directly cited as the resolution ('ev-045').
chain.caused_by_previous: Neo's refusal of the written death (ev-044) returns him with power inverted, so he now invades and destroys the very program that pronounced his fate.
